lessonRef.unitTitle: PF7 — Paying Taxes: Tax Structure, Withholding, and Filing
lessonRef.title: Concept model A: payroll taxes and employer withholding

objective: Compute payroll tax for two fictional wage levels under a schedule with a wage cap on one levy and none on the other, and show that the combined rate falls as wages rise past the cap.
scenario: The simulated payroll levies below are invented for this exercise. In this fictional system the social insurance levy is 6% of wages up to a cap of $158,000, and the health levy is 1.5% of all wages with no cap. These are separate from the income tax and are withheld from every paycheck.
safetyNotes: Every figure, person, employer, institution, offer, account, and document on this task sheet is fictional and exists only for practice.
No real transaction is part of this lesson, and no real bank, card, brokerage, tax, or login detail is ever requested. If a task sheet ever appears to ask for one, stop and tell a trusted adult.
This lesson teaches general financial concepts and does not advise anyone about their own money. For a real decision, talk with a trusted adult or a qualified licensed professional.
materials: the fictional payroll schedule in these directions

tasks.directions: Worker A earns wages of $58,000 in the simulated year, which is below the $158,000 social insurance cap. Compute each levy separately. Note that no deduction applies to payroll tax in this system: the levies are charged on wages from the first dollar.

prompts.text: What is Worker A’s social insurance levy?
What is Worker A’s health levy?
What is Worker A’s total payroll tax?

tasks.directions: Worker B earns wages of $210,000 in the same year, which is above the cap. Apply the cap to the social insurance levy only.

prompts.text: What is Worker B’s social insurance levy?
What is Worker B’s health levy?
What is Worker B’s total payroll tax?
What share of Worker B’s wages is that?
What share of Worker A’s wages was their payroll tax?

The income tax in the previous lesson took a larger share as income rose; this payroll tax takes a smaller one. Explain what feature of each schedule produces that difference, and say why a person comparing two jobs should look at both taxes rather than the income tax alone.

remediation: If Worker B’s social insurance levy comes out as $12,600, the 6% is being charged on the whole $210,000. The cap stops that levy at $158,000 of wages, so the charge is 6% of $158,000. The health levy is the one with no cap, and it does apply to all $210,000.
extension: Find the wage level at which the combined payroll rate first falls below 7%, and say what happens to that rate as wages continue to rise.
